newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen B shares end firmer on road company IPO.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen B shares end firmer on road company IPO.

text.p: Shenzhen's B share index closed up on Tuesday on confidence over China's economic outlook lifted by the successful initial public offering of Shenzhen Expressway Co Ltd in Hong Kong, brokers said.
The B share index gained 0.92 points or 0.59 percent to close at 157.34, with turnover jumping to HK$95 million from Monday's HK$55 million.
The IPO of the Shenzhen Expressway's 650 million H shares was 37 times over-subscribed by foreign investors, the Shenzhen-based Securities Times said on Tuesday.
The company offered 10 percent of the issue at HK$2.20 per share to the Hong Kong public and 90 percent to institutional investors, the newspaper said.
"Today's market was pushed up by foreign buyers, excited by the Shenzhen Expressway's successful IPO," a trader with Southern China Securities Co said.
"Buying was quite active today, which showed confidence in China's economic prospects," he said.
Analysts said they expected the market to maintain upward momentum over the next few days, but gains would be limited with institutions cautious in the corporate reporting season.
Appliance maker Tsann Kuen was the best performer on institutional buying, advancing HK$0.15 or 3.88 percent to HK$4.02 on trade of 1.04 milli on shares.
Guangdong Provincial Expressway Development Co added HK$0.29 or 3.41 percent to HK$8.79 on volume of 244,500 shares.
Building materials producer Shenzhen Fangda traded most on 2.04 million shares but dropped HK$0.05 to HK$9.09 after an intraday low of HK$8.35.
An analyst said "the fall was linked to concerns about the company's 1997 earnings, which are likely to be diluted if the firm issues 30 million more B shares."

The A share index rose 7.82 points or 1.94 percent to 409.97 on turnover of 9.34 billion yuan, compared with 7.00 billion on Monday. Buying focused on stocks said to be planning good dividends, brokers said.
Chemical fibre maker Meilun Co closed the session at its 10-percent limit-up of 10.20 yuan after 4.10 million shares were traded.
